input:
This executive summary provides an overview of delivery performance at a contract packaging firm that operates 4 plants and generates revenue of $117 million per year, and it considers a recommendation that has been put forward in response to ongoing challenges in meeting delivery commitments. The analysis draws on order records for 12 months, comprising 11852 orders in total.

Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery stood at 91%, which falls short of the target of 95% that the firm has set for itself. A closer look at the data reveals that Plant 2 accounts for 63% of all late orders, highlighting the extent to which the issue is concentrated in a single location. Meanwhile, overtime cost reached $2.4 million last year, up 18% on the year before, and the order backlog currently stands at 3.8 weeks, compared with 1.9 weeks a year ago, underscoring the growing pressure on the operation.

A scheduling system for all plants has been quoted at $339k, while Plant 2 alone would cost $120k. An internal estimate — it should be noted that this is not a vendor figure — suggests that the overtime reduction at Plant 2 could be in the region of 15% to 20% in the first year. Against this backdrop, the recommendation under consideration is to install the system at Plant 2 first and to hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported, thereby allowing the firm to validate the expected benefits before committing further. The operations director owns the scheduling programme and will oversee its implementation going forward.
